Flooding Disrupts Luxembourg Media & Publishing Industry Operations

Heavy rainfall has led to severe flooding across several key sites of Luxembourg’s Media & Publishing industry, disrupting the operations of major firms and affecting hundreds of workers. The event, which began late Monday night and intensified through Tuesday, has inundated publishing plants and media offices in the outskirts of Luxembourg City and the Grevenmacher region.

The headquarters of LuxPress Editions, a leading publisher, reported significant water damage to its printing facility. "Our main plant floor is under nearly half a metre of water," said Henri Müller, operations manager. "We have halted all production for the safety of our staff, and it is unclear when we will be able to resume."

Floodwaters have also reached the premises of Nouvelle Voix Media Group, where the company’s newsrooms and archives are located. Employees were evacuated early Tuesday morning as rising water levels threatened electrical systems and valuable records. "We are working to secure our archives and safeguard our digital infrastructure," stated Céline Gruber, communications director. "Staff safety is our top priority."

According to the Luxembourg Media & Publishing Workers’ Union, as many as 300 employees across various sites have been asked to stay home or assist in emergency measures. "Some workers are helping move equipment to higher floors, while others are awaiting further instructions," said union representative Marc Hoffmann.

The Luxembourg Federation of Publishers estimates that at least 40 percent of industry sites in affected areas have reported some level of disruption as the flooding continues. "We are monitoring the situation hour by hour," said the Federation’s president, Anne Weber, urging all industry staff to follow safety guidance until the waters recede.
